delayedFeedback.title: Delayed Feedback
delayedFeedback.description: Practice speaking and receive audio feedback
delayedFeedback.headerDescription: Delayed Auditory Feedback (DAF) tool for speech fluency practice
delayedFeedback.effectsStabilityBody: For stability on Bluetooth headsets, delay and pitch are disabled. You can enable effects on non‑Bluetooth (wired/USB) routes.
delayedFeedback.whyItWorksBody: Delayed Auditory Feedback can induce fluency in many (though not all) people who stutter by altering auditory timing and speech motor control.
delayedFeedback.detailBody: Research suggests subgroup differences in responsiveness to DAF, potentially related to auditory association cortex asymmetries. Your experience may vary; try different delay settings.

choralSpeaking.title: Choral Speaking
choralSpeaking.description: Speak together with a TTS voice to build fluency.
choralSpeaking.headphoneHint: For best sync, use headphones and a quiet room.
choralSpeaking.source2: Choral speech neurobiology and fluency effects (2003)
choralSpeaking.summaryBody: Choral speaking improves fluency by synchronizing your speech timing and prosody to a clear external model voice, which reduces the degrees of freedom in speech motor planning, strengthens auditory–motor coupling, and dampens maladaptive self‑monitoring—together stabilizing forward flow of articulation. Benefits are greatest when the reference is intelligible and temporally aligned, with moderate rates that preserve clarity.
choralSpeaking.detailBody: Timing alignment provides strong external cues for initiation and pacing, while intelligible prosody supports modeling of stress and rhythm. Moderate speaking rates preserve clarity and make synchrony easier, which together reduce stuttering frequency in choral contexts.
